h: Airport History and a Market with Centuries Behind It
p: Croydon has been a market town for centuries, and Surrey Street Market is still going strong, a short walk from Centrale. It's a great spot for fresh fruit, cheap eats and a bit of local colour. Just down the road, Croydon Minster is the historic parish church where several Archbishops of Canterbury are buried.

Here's a fact that surprises a lot of people: Croydon was home to London's main airport before Heathrow. The original terminal building, Airport House, still stands on Purley Way, and the Croydon Airport Visitor Centre opens on selected days to show off the history of early air travel. It's a brilliant one for aviation-mad kids.

Croydon's walls are a gallery in their own right too. The town has a growing collection of large murals painted by street artists, and spotting them as you walk around is a fun game for older children.
For views, head to Addington Hills, where a viewing platform looks out over the London skyline, all the way to the City and Canary Wharf. It's a cracking spot on a clear day.
Closer to the centre, Wandle Park is a smaller green space where the River Wandle has been brought back to the surface, with a play area and space to run about.
The Museum of Croydon, in the Clocktower building, is free and tells the stories of local people through the decades.
With all of this within easy reach, Croydon makes a much more interesting day out than many expect.
Being so well connected, it's also an easy one for grandparents to meet you at, wherever they're coming from.
